segments.now: Talking with Ramesh and Shri G. Hegde at home.

entries.text: Morning papers: “Rainfall expected in Tamil Nadu as depression to turn severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal by November 17” · “2.5 kg gold, 1.6 kg silver, Rs 26 lakh seized from raids on Madhya Pradesh officer” · “Flight services on Imphal-Silchar route scheduled to commence on November 24”

items.intention: Address Ramesh regarding the arrears and the impossibility of immediate payment with my current cash.
Explain to Ramesh that the wage for cooking is suspended until funds are available, refusing to borrow against vouchers.
Walk to Lodhi Gardens to clear my head and observe the tension between the dream and the state.
Return home to face the empty pot, acknowledging the physical limit of my philosophical freedom.
Sit with the newspaper and reflect on the cyclone in the Bay of Bengal as a natural force indifferent to history.
Write a letter to the Directorate of Estates inquiring about the status of the file and the release of funds.

entries.text: Ramesh stands before me, the embodiment of the immediate need that my universal poverty cannot meet. I hold six rupees against a debt of four thousand; the ethical idea of the state is suspended in the gap between my pen and his hunger. I must speak with the clarity of a man who understands that the particular will cannot be satisfied by the universal reason when the purse is empty, for the body does not wait for the dialectic to resolve itself.

Ramesh, I see you, and I see the weight of what you ask. But look at my hand: here are six rupees, the totality of my particular existence at this hour. The state's money is in the Directorate's keeping, and my own is in the future. I cannot cook, for I cannot pay you, and I cannot pay you, for I am a man of reason without the means of sense. The wage for cooking is suspended, as is the grocery, until the file returns on the twentieth. Do not wait for me; the pot remains empty, and so shall I, until the spirit of the treasury moves.
Chau ka paisa? Aur bhaav-bhaan? File wapas aayegi toh pet bhi wapas aayega? Main abhi chalta hoon, kal subah aakar dekho.

Ramesh leaves with the papers, his hunger a concrete demand my abstract poverty cannot answer. Hegde remains, the true owner of this house, watching my humiliation with the calm of a man who has no such debts. The tension is clear: the state, which should be the actuality of the ethical idea, has failed me, leaving me to the mercy of a caretaker's patience and a bureaucrat's indifference.

Shri Hegde, the file is gone for orders, and with it, my means of subsistence. Ramesh has left; there is no food, and no money to buy any. The system of needs operates with a cold logic that my philosophy cannot soothe. I am, for now, a body without resources in a house that is not mine.

Well, if you are that hungry, eat the biscuits from the cupboard, I will not stop you. But do not make a philosophy out of my empty fridge, Shri Hegel, just find a way to feed yourself or I am leaving.

Ramesh asks for ₹4,000 (the wage for cooking, three days a week), and you have only ₹6. Ramesh asks for ₹1,500 (groceries), and you have only ₹6. The electricity company asks for ₹1,800 (electricity), and you have only ₹6. The dhobi asks for ₹300 (the washing), and you have only ₹6. Ramesh is here.

shelf_exposure.text: Bumps and hollows, there is room for selection! And again his murderous propensity can be referred to some bump or hollow or another, and this in turn to some mental quahty or another; for the murderer is neither this abstract of a murderer, nor does he have merely one protuberance and one depression.

Official position is not based upon contract (§ 75), although it involves the consent of the two sides and also a double performance. The public servant is not called to a single chance act of service, as is the attorney, but finds in his work the main interest of both his spiritual and his particular existence.

shelf_exposure.text: Such an association is occasioned by needs, and is preserved by the law, which secures one's person and property, and by an external system for private and common interests. O. This external state goes back to, and finds its central principle in, the end and actuality of the substantive universal, and of the public life dedicated to the maintenance of the universal.

Was sich wirklich im Staate geltend macht, muß sich freilich auf organische Weise betätigen, und dies ist in der Verfassung der Fall. Aber zu allen Zeiten war die öffentliche Meinung eine große Macht und ist es besonders in unserer Zeit, wo das Prinzip der subjektiven Freiheit diese Wichtigkeit und Bedeutung hat.

works.title: On the Ethical Substance and the Dream of the East
works.tail: dead. They are the work of a spirit that has not yet woken up. I must continue. The night is long, and the haze is thick. But the mind must move, even if the body is still. Even if the air is unbreathable. The spirit does not breathe; it thinks. And in thinking, it is free. Even in the dream. Especially in the dream. For the dream is the only place where the spirit can see itself clearly, before it is crushed by the weight of the actual. I shall continue my notes. The letter is done. The notes are not. The notes are the work of the spirit. The letter is the work of the clerk. I am no clerk. I am the philosopher. And the philosopher must see the whole. The whole is the dream. And the dream is the truth. Until the state wakes up. Until the brown haze clears. Until the spirit becomes free.

works.title: Letter to the Directorate of Estates
works.to: The Officer in Charge, Directorate of Estates
works.tail:
state ought to be.

I request that the necessary corrections be made to the files so that the residence may be formally allocated to its proper occupant. In the interim, I shall continue to manage the household affairs, including the payment of the dhobi and the electricity, using the imprest funds provided. I am careful to distinguish between the state’s money, which requires vouchers, and my own cash, which is limited. This distinction is vital; the ethical fabric of the household, like that of the state, depends on the clear separation of particular and universal duties.

I trust this matter will be resolved in the course of the day, as all particulars must resolve into the universal. I remain, with respect, your obedient servant,

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
Resident, Tughlak Road
